rationale: Verification and stopping record, with no new records. Both investigations of this run are complete and their accounts consistent: the configuration-recovery question (98ee8dfd5fac4b84915f91ed4b094bcf-question-0) rests on six receipts - the four single-voter recovery cases with their flag-off controls, the three-voter commit-rule witness, the durable-snapshot corruption and its flag-off restart, and the authority pair with both a repeat that lacked its premise and a revised execution that enforces it - and the replay-completion question (29e4214f5ee146b393957fa23a33a73d-question-0) rests on nine receipts covering the block, the measured bound, the exact 128-versus-129 boundary, the default-configuration reachability and the availability consequence, each reproduced at least twice with identical operands. A final consistency check of 42 claims across 13 receipts against the retained observations found no discrepancy, and both knowledge corrections raised by this evidence - the tuple-counted batching and the randomized snapshot cadence - are recorded with their affected uses marked and their gaps answered. The remaining limitations are structural to the harness (in-memory transports and stores in one process, no production store, no process-level restart or disk fault) and cannot be removed in the remaining allocation without leaving an uncited receipt, so no further work is initiated.
